title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: The continuous-batcher scheduler has been optimized incrementally (see earlier PRs pr-53984, pr-52341, pr-51234) but we observed two recurring issues in high-concurrency workloads: (1) small/low-cost requests experiencing starvation behind long-running batches, and (2) occasional queue head-of-line blocking when a single slow task exceeds expected completion time, degrading tail latency. This PR introduces scheduler-level mitigations for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and configurable timeouts. Changes include: 1) admission/priority aging: requests are assigned a priority class based on estimated token length and time-in-queue; an aging factor gradually increments priority to guarantee eventual service for long-waiting small requests; 2) per-request soft timeouts + evacuation: tasks that exceed a configurable soft timeout are evicted from a batch and requeued with boosted priority to avoid head-of-line blocking; 3) bounded queue slices: instead of allowing unbounded head accumulation we partition the pending queue into fixed-size slices to limit how long a single class can occupy the head; 4) starvation detector and fast-path for tiny requests: when starvation heuristics trigger (high mean wait + skew), tiny requests (<32 tokens estimate) get a prioritized fast-path batch; 5) observability hooks: metrics for queue_wait_seconds_by_priority, evictions_total, starvation_events_total, and detailed tracing spans for admission decisions. Implementation notes: - Scheduler changes are in runtime/batcher/scheduler.go and runtime/batcher/queue.go - KV cache interaction: eviction+requeue preserves KV cache references to avoid re-populating KV on re-run; see runtime/kv/cache.go changes - Config: new batcher tuning knobs added to pkg/config/batcher.yaml with sane defaults and safety caps - Tests: added unit and integration tests (tests/batcher/*) and a distributed load bench harness (benchmarks/continuous-batcher/bench_v2) Performance: microbenching under a mixed workload (30% tiny <32 tokens, 50% medium 32-512, 20% long >512) with 8xA100 equivalent machines showed: - steady-state throughput +9-12% (dependant on model size and sequence length) - p95 latency reduction for tiny requests: 18-25% under high load - reduction in starvation events: ~98% fewer detected cases in the bench harness Safety and rollout: default config keeps existing behavior; new tuning knobs are opt-in via feature flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2. Rollout plan: start with canary on Dedicated pools (10% traffic) for 48 hours, then 50% for 24 hours, then full rollout. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for scheduler logic - [x] Integration tests with KV cache preservation - [x] Benchmarks comparing prior and new scheduler - [x] Docs: add notes to runtime/batcher/README.md - [x] Add metrics and tracing spans - [x] Feature flag gated for gradual rollout Related: ENG-7432 (fairness tuning), SUP-1124 (support case where small requests starved), pr-53984 and pr-52341 for earlier scheduler work. Notes for reviewers: focus review on scheduler.go and queue.go changes; pay attention to concurrency invariants and correct reference preservation in kv/cache.go. This description is intentionally verbose to record rationale and rollout guidance.
